title: Special Order for Louisiana Public Service Commission ex parte. — This Special Order accepts the Annual Report of the Louisiana Utilities Restoration Corporation for the fiscal year 2025.

documents.text:
LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                          ORDER NUMBER 73-2026


Docket Nos. U-29203, U-30981, U-32764, U-35991, and U-36350, Discussion and possible vote
to accept and approve the Annual Report of the Louisiana Utilities Restoration Corporation to
the LPSC for the fiscal year 2025, including the annual Operating Budget for fiscal year 2026
and the iterim and annual Compiled Financial Statements for fiscal year 2025.

                  (Decided at the October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)

         This matter is before the Louisiana Public Service Commission (“LPSC” or
“Commission”) to accept and approve the Annual Report of the Louisiana Utilities Restoration
Corporation (“LURC”) for the fiscal year 2026 Annual Report, including the interim and annual
Compiled Financial Statements for fiscal year ending June 30, 2026 and the Annual Operating
Budget for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027. The LURC’s Annual Report reports on the status
of and ongoing compliance activities in connection to the Joint Applications of Entergy Gulf States
Louisiana, L.L.C. (“EGSL”) and Entergy Louisiana, LLC (“ELL”) (collectively, “Entergy”)1 for
recovery in rates of costs related to Hurricanes Katrina and Rita,2 Gustav and Ike,3 Isaac,4 Laura,
Delta, Zeta and Winter Storm Uri,5 and Hurricane Ida.6 Further, the Annual Report reported on
the status of Entergy New Orleans’ storm reserve fund securitization.
         Act 55 of the 2007 Legislative Session, as amended by Act 293 of the 2021 Louisiana
Regular Legislative Session, (now codified as La. R.S. 45:1311-1328, the “Act”) created the
LURC, a nonprofit public corporation regulated by the LPSC for the purpose of assisting in the
securitization process with respect to system restoration costs incurred by utilities as a result of
hurricanes or other natural disasters. Pursuant to the Act, as well as LPSC Order Nos. U-29203,
U-30981, U-32764, U-35991, and U-36350, the LURC’s Board of Directors is required to submit
its fiscal year annual report to the Commission for review and approval.
         The LPSC issued Financing Orders with respect to the Katrina/Rita, Gustav/Ike, Isaac, and
Laura/Delta/Zeta/Winter Storm Uri, and Hurricane Ida transactions (“Financing Orders”), each of
which authorized the LURC, pursuant to the provisions of the Act, to borrow the proceeds of
system restoration bonds in one or more series (the “Bonds”) to finance non-shareholder capital
contributions to EGSL and ELL related to EGSL’s and ELL’s interim and/or permanent system
restoration costs, carrying costs on such system restoration costs, re-establishing and replenishing
storm damage reserves, and issuance costs of the Bonds.
         The LURC Board of Directors submitted its fiscal year 2026 Annual Report to the
Commission on September 25, 2026. Therein, the LURC Board reported on the following topics:
1. Status of and ongoing compliance activities related to the Entergy Louisiana, LLC/Entergy
   Gulf States Louisiana Katrina/Rita, Gustav/Ike, Isaac, and Entergy Louisiana (“ELL”) Laura,
   Delta, Zeta, Winter Storm Uri and Hurricane Ida securitizations;

1 On October 1, 2015, pursuant to LPSC Order No. U-33244-A, Entergy Gulf States Louisiana, L.L.C. combined

substantially all of their respective assets and liabilities (the “Business Combination”) into a single operating company,
Entergy Louisiana Power, LLC, which subsequently changed its name to Entergy Louisiana, LLC (“ELL”).
2
  LPSC Docket No. U-29203.
3 LPSC Docket No. U-30981.
4 LPSC Docket No. U-32764.
5 LPSC Docket No. U-35991.
6 LPSC Docket No. U-36350.

                                                                                                            Page 1
 2. Status of and ongoing compliance activities related to the Entergy New Orleans (ENO) storm
   reserve fund securitization;
3. Status of reports from and submissions to the Louisiana Legislative Auditor and the Division
   of Administration’s Office of Statewide Reporting and Accounting Policy;
4. Ongoing activities required to maintain LURC’s corporate status; and,
5. Matters reported to the LURC Board of Directors during the Fiscal Year ending June 30, 2026

COMMISSION CONSIDERATION
       After discussion, on motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Commissioner Lewis, and
unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to accept and approve the Fiscal Year 2026 Annual
Report of the LURC to the Commission, including the Annual Operating Budget for the fiscal
year ending June 30, 2027 and interim and compiled annual financial statements for the fiscal year
ending June 30, 2026.


THEREFORE, IT IS ORDERED:
       The Fiscal Year 2026 Annual Report of the LURC is accepted.
This Order is effective immediately.

BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA
November 20, 2026
